title: 2008 HMMT February Algebra Problem 2
statement: Let \(f(n)\) be the number of times you have to hit the \(\sqrt{ }\) key on a calculator to get a number less than 2 starting from \(n\). For instance, \(f(2)=1, f(5)=2\). For how many \(1<m<2008\) is \(f(m)\) odd?

solutions.text: 242 This is \(\left[2^{1}, 2^{2}\right) \cup\left[2^{4}, 2^{8}\right) \cup\left[2^{16}, 2^{32}\right) \ldots\), and \(2^{8}<2008<2^{16}\) so we have exactly the first two intervals.
